### Organization chart
A reporting line drawn top down, with each person as a card under their manager.

Component ID: `org-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/org-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/org-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.15.0)

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `native`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Example: Twelve people in four teams under a CIO are an org chart. Three hundred employees someone needs to search are a data table with a manager column.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Upstream: web-extension-inventory-reviewed (2026-10-16); [evidence](https://m3.material.io/components).

Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. The inventory page renders client-side, so this review relies on the 2026-09-13 inventory review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

Support (2026-10-16, `llm.md#organization-chart`): Nested lists of native disclosures drawn as cards under their manager, with connector lines, a role band, an avatar and a name, profile links on cards without reports, mirrored order in RTL and sideways scrolling when wide.

Web adaptation: Native <details> managers and nested lists; every manager is a Tab stop and no tree role is promised.

Known boundary: Cards side by side under their manager in LTR and RTL, the connector bar and drops, a wide chart scrolling with its start reachable, Enter folding a team away, the caret under reduced motion, the caret in forced colors in Chromium and the nested lists in the accessibility tree are checked in a browser; spoken output, the rest of forced colors and enlarged text remain unverified.

Full parity remains unassessed. [Capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#org-chart).

#### Contract

A `<ul class="org-chart">` nests lists, one `<li>` per person. A person with reports holds a `<details open>`: its `<summary class="org-chart-node">` is the card and its nested `<ul>` the reports, so the browser folds a team away. A person without reports holds a `<div class="org-chart-node">`, or an `<a class="org-chart-node">` to their profile. A card stacks an optional `.org-chart-role` band, which must come first, an `.avatar` and an `.org-chart-name`. The stylesheet draws the connecting lines. CSS only.

#### Syntax

```html
<ul class="org-chart" aria-label="Company staff">
  <li>
    <details open>
      <summary class="org-chart-node">
        <span class="org-chart-role">CIO</span>
        <img class="avatar large" src="marisol.jpg" alt="">
        <span class="org-chart-name">Marisol Okafor</span>
      </summary>
      <ul>
        <li>
          <div class="org-chart-node">
            <span class="org-chart-role">R&amp;D</span>
            <span class="avatar large" aria-hidden="true">IH</span>
            <span class="org-chart-name">Ingrid Halvorsen</span>
          </div>
        </li>
      </ul>
    </details>
  </li>
</ul>
```

#### Also documented

The Organization chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `org-chart-is-not-a-tree-widget`: A .org-chart takes no ARIA tree roles. It is lists of disclosures, which keep their own roles and keyboard behavior.
- `org-chart-manager-holds-no-link`: A manager's card is the summary that opens the team, so a link or button inside it competes with that. Link the profile elsewhere; only a card without reports can be an <a class="org-chart-node">.
